THE YMCA YEAR BOOK IS READABLE FROM HERE — EVERY YEAR THIS PROJECT CALLED MISSING
==================================================================================
Compiled 2026-09-07. THIS FILE SUPERSEDES THE ACCESS-FAILURE VERDICT IN
2026-09-06-hathitrust-holdings-the-missing-years.txt AND THE CLOSING PARAGRAPH OF
2026-09-06-complete-ia-inventory-of-the-series.txt. Both remain accurate about the Internet
Archive and about HathiTrust. Both were wrong about the conclusion drawn from them, which was
that this environment cannot read the missing years. It can.

WHAT WAS WRONG WITH YESTERDAY'S VERDICT
---------------------------------------
Yesterday's note listed four routes to the 1901-1905 and 1910-1920 volumes and found three shut
(HathiTrust behind Cloudflare, Google Books behind a quota, the Data API behind OAuth). The
fourth was written down as "the Kautz Family YMCA Archives, University of Minnesota, WHICH HOLDS
THE SERIES IN PRINT." That last clause was an assumption, not a finding. Nobody had asked
Minnesota whether it also holds the series digitally. It does, and the digital copy is open.

Retried first, for the record, because the note said to: Google Books still returns HTTP 429,
and the quota message names THE SAME consumer project number as yesterday. That reframes it —
it is a shared key exhausted by other traffic, not a daily allowance that resets for this
session, so "retry tomorrow" is not the fix. books.google.com and google.com/search?tbm=bks both
302 to /sorry/index, Google's bot wall. babel.hathitrust.org is still the Cloudflare
interstitial. So three of yesterday's four routes are shut today as well; only the untested
assumption gave way.

THE ROUTE THAT WORKS
--------------------
University of Minnesota Libraries, collection "YMCA Yearbooks, Directories, and Proceedings",
ContentDM alias p16022coll351 on cdm16022.contentdm.oclc.org. 173 items. Finding aid:
https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/883

Two endpoints, both answering normally from this environment:

  ENUMERATE / FULL-TEXT SEARCH
  https://cdm16022.contentdm.oclc.org/digital/bl/dmwebservices/index.php?q=
      dmQuery/p16022coll351/<searchstring>/title!dmrecord/nosort/<rows>/<start>/0/0/0/json
  searchstring is either 0 (everything) or FIELD^TERMS^MODE^OPERATOR, e.g.
      CISOSEARCHALL^Kanawana^all^and          (all words)
      CISOSEARCHALL^Harold C. Cross^exact^and (exact phrase — verified working)
  Hits come back AT PAGE LEVEL, each carrying parentobject = the volume's dmrecord.

  READ ONE PAGE'S OCR
  ...index.php?q=dmGetItemInfo/p16022coll351/<page dmrecord>/json
  The OCR is the "transc" field. NOTE: cdmhasocr reads 0 on pages that plainly have OCR in
  transc, so DO NOT USE cdmhasocr TO DECIDE WHETHER A PAGE IS READABLE. Read transc.

  UMedia's own search.json (umedia.lib.umn.edu) also answers but IGNORES the set_spec and
  facets parameters — it returned Social Work Year Books and county maps for collection-scoped
  queries. Use ContentDM directly.

EVERY HOLE IS HERE, WITH ITS RECORD NUMBER
------------------------------------------
The years the Internet Archive lacks entirely, and the three HathiTrust also lacks (starred):

  1883        2255        1909-10     11112
  1901        13624       1910-11     5935
  1902        13285       1911-12     9872
  1902-03     14318       1912-13 *   5467
  1903-04     14699       1913-14     5052
  1904-05     1059        1914-15 *   6336
  1905-06     8010        1915-16     9113
                          1916-17     3985
                          1917-18     15936
                          1918-19     15358
                          1919-20     16539
                          1920-21 *   34602

The collection also runs forward through 1982 (the 1957-1968 volumes are what carry Kanawana;
see below), and holds 1885 and 1889 — the remaining two nineteenth-century holes — is NOT
established here and was not checked.

OCR COVERAGE WAS CONTROLLED BEFORE ANY NULL WAS TRUSTED
-------------------------------------------------------
A full-text search for "Montreal" returns 2,742 page hits across 124 distinct volumes, and
EVERY ONE of the nineteen target volumes above appears among them. So these volumes are OCR'd
and searchable, and a null in them is a null in the book rather than a hole in the scanning.
That control is what makes the two nulls recorded below worth anything.


FINDING 1 — "KANAWANA" APPEARS IN THIS SERIES ONLY FROM 1957 TO 1968
=====================================================================
Seventeen pages, in eleven volumes: 1957, 1958, 1959, 1960, 1961, 1963, 1964, 1965, 1966, 1967,
1968. Not once before 1957 and not once after 1968, across a series running 1877-1982.

THAT IS A NULL ABOUT THE NATIONAL ROSTER, NOT ABOUT THE CAMP. What changes in the late 1950s is
almost certainly the roster's own practice — camps start being listed as posts within a
metropolitan board — not anything about Kanawana, which had been running for sixty years by
then. Do not read the 1894-1956 silence as evidence of anything except that this particular
publication did not name camps.

The camp is spelled "Kamp Kanawana" in the roster from 1957 through 1965 and "Camp Kanawana"
from 1966. This project already knows the K spelling well; it is recorded here only because the
changeover year is clean in this series.

THE DIRECTOR SERIES, VERBATIM FROM THE QUEBEC BLOCK OF THE DIRECTORY OF ASSOCIATIONS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1957  "Assistant Program, Kamp Kanawana, Murray B. Shantz"      (Montreal Metro. Bd.)
1958  "Assistant Program, Kamp Kanawana, Murray B. Shantz"
1959  "Assistant Program, Kamp Kanawana, A. Ross Seaman"
1960  "Program, Kamp Kanawana, A. Ross Seaman"
1961  "Program, Kamp Kanawana, A. Ross Seaman"
1963  "Program, Kamp Kanawana, A. Ross Seaman"
1964  "Program, Kamp Kanawana, A. Ross Seaman"
1965  "Program, Kamp Kanawana, A. Ross Seaman"
1966  "Program, Camp Kanawana, A. Ross Seaman"
1967  "Program, Camp Kanawana, A. Ross Seaman"
1968  "Program, Camp Kanawana, A. Ross Seaman"

1962 IS ABSENT FROM THE HIT LIST and it is not clear whether the 1962 volume is in this
collection at all — that was not checked. Do not record 1962 as a null until it is.

WHY THIS MATTERS TO THE WIKI, PRECISELY
  - directors-index.md carries Shantz at 1955-1958 with "1956-1958 is inference from that
    silence" — inference from the Montreal annual reports NOT recording a change. The 1957 and
    1958 Year Books state him in the post outright, from outside Montreal's own paper. Two of
    those three inferred years become documented.
  - The same index says of 1968: "Summer 1968 has no named on-site director anywhere — not in
    the annual report, not in any 1968 news release or newsletter." The 1968 Year Book names
    Seaman in the Kanawana post. READ IT CAREFULLY BEFORE CLAIMING TOO MUCH: this is the
    Metropolitan Board's staff roster and gives him the camp, exactly as it does for 1966 and
    1967; it does not use the words "on-site director," and the index's own warning about the
    branch-officers table — that the man holding the camping portfolio is not always the man on
    site — applies here with equal force. What it establishes is that a national publication
    put Seaman in the Kanawana post for 1968. It does not establish who ran the 1968 season on
    the ground.
  - Seaman's own entry line in the alphabetical list of employed officers gives his year of
    entry into Association work as 53, and the 1957 and 1958 volumes place him at "Montreal,
    Que., Lachine, Exec" — Executive of the Lachine YMCA in the two years before he took the
    camp. The index says only "career in community work preceded directorship."
  - Shantz's entry line gives his year of entry as 46, and the 1959 and later volumes show him
    at "Toronto, Ont., Sec. National Council" — corroborating the index's "left in 1959 for the
    YMCA National Council staff" from an independent source.
  - Camp Otoreke: "Dir. Camp Otoreke, Clarence J. McGerrigle" 1957-1961, and "Program, Camp
    Otoreke, Colin R. McKay" 1963-1965. COLIN R. McKAY OCCURS NOWHERE IN THIS PROJECT — checked
    by grep across wiki, kb, project-docs and the source index before writing this line.


FINDING 2 — W. J. HOLLIDAY DID NOT GET THE BOYS' WORK DIRECTORSHIP BACK
========================================================================
This was question 1 on yesterday's list, and the answer is no. He goes sideways into branch
administration and stays there for at least seven years.

  1909-10  Montreal, Central Dept.: "Asst., (Memb.,) W. J. Holliday" — a membership assistant.
  1910-11  "Fairmount Ave. Br., Ch., W. A. Wilson / Secy., W. J. Holliday"
  1911-12  "North Br., Chairman, W. A. Wilson / Secy., W. J. Holliday"
  1912-13  "North Br. ... Secy., W. J. Holliday"
  1913-14  "North Br., Chairman, H. R. MacGregor / Secy., W. J. Holliday"
  1914-15  "North Br., 2300 Park Ave., Chairman, George S. Rorke / Secy., W. J. Holliday"
  1915-16  "North Br., 2300 Park Ave., Chairman, George S. Rorke / Secy., W. J. Holliday"
  1916-17  "North Br., 2300 Park Ave., Chairman, S. W. Cuthbert / Secy., W. J. Holliday"

The Fairmount Avenue branch of 1910-11 and the North Branch of 1911 onward share a chairman
(W. A. Wilson) and a secretary (Holliday) across the changeover, which suggests the same branch
under a new name at 2300 Park Ave. THAT IS AN INFERENCE FROM TWO NAMES AND IS NOT STATED
ANYWHERE IN THESE VOLUMES.

AND THE MONTREAL BOYS' WORK POST ITSELF, YEAR BY YEAR — yesterday's question 2, the closest
thing to a list of the men over the camp through the new site's first decade:

  1910-11  Central Dept., "Boys, Kenneth J. Hollinshead"
  1911-12  Central Dept., "Boys, Kenneth J. Hollinshead"
  1912-13  Central Dept., "Boys, D. J. Evans" (with "Asst. Boys, H. A. Lordly")
  1913-14  Central Dept., "Boys, D. J. Evans"
  1914-15  Central Br., "Boys," — THE LINE IS PRINTED WITH NO NAME AFTER IT
  1915-16  Central Br., "Boys, John G. MacKinnon"
  1916-17  Central Br., "Boys, John G. MacKinnon"

KENNETH J. HOLLINSHEAD OCCURS NOWHERE IN THIS PROJECT; so does no Percy D. Brandon and no
Arthur L. Walsh. All three checked by grep before writing.

A CAUTION THAT MATTERS FOR THE CAMP. These are the CENTRAL DEPARTMENT / CENTRAL BRANCH boys'
workers. The 1909-10 volume prints "Boys' Work Dir." as a separate line from the branch "Boys"
lines, which means the association-level directorship and a branch boys' post are not the same
office. Whether the man who ran Kanawana in these years is the Central Branch's boys' worker,
an association-level Boys' Work Director, or someone the Year Book does not list at all is NOT
settled by any of the above. What is settled is that Holliday was not it.


FINDING 3 — WHERE HAROLD C. CROSS WAS BETWEEN 1912 AND 1919
============================================================
wiki/people/harold-cross.md states the question in those words: his 1921 entry-year figure of
"12" is "seven years earlier than any date this article had, and it opens a question that did
not exist before: where was he between 1912 and 1919?" Five of those years now have an answer,
and the first three of them say Montreal.

  1911-12  "North Br. ... Physical, W. S. Maguire / Boys, Harold C. Cross"      MONTREAL
  1912-13  "North Br. ... Physical, W. S. Maguire / Boys, Harold C. Cross"      MONTREAL
  1913-14  "North Br. ... Physical, W. S. Maguire / Boys, Harold C. Cross"      MONTREAL
  1914-15  "Prince Edward Island / Charlottetown ... Gen. Secy., Harold C. Cross"
  1915-16  Charlottetown's General Secretary is J. Morrison Clark. Cross is gone.
  1915-16, 1916-17, 1917-18  ABSENT — an exact-phrase search for "Harold C. Cross" returns no
           page in any of these three volumes, which ARE OCR'd (see the control above).
  1918-19  "Victoria. President, / Gen. Secy., J. M. Graham / Asst., Harry H. Hollins /
            Physical, James Thompson / Boys, Harold C. Cross"                   VICTORIA, B.C.
  1920-21  "Victoria. President, George McGregor / Gen. Secy., J. M. Graham / ...
            Physical, W. S. Maguire / Boys, Harold C. Cross"                    VICTORIA, B.C.

SO: a Montreal YMCA boys' worker at the North Branch for three years in the early 1910s, more
than a decade before he directed Kanawana; then General Secretary at Charlottetown for a year;
then unfound for three volumes; then Boys' Work at Victoria, where the article already had him
from 1919 on a Concordia source. The Victoria years are now corroborated from outside Concordia.

TWO THINGS TO HOLD LOOSELY HERE.
1. The three absent volumes are a null in this series, not a finding about his whereabouts.
   The obvious guess is war service and the obvious check is a CEF service file, but this
   document does not support the guess and it is not recorded as a fact.
2. The entry-year figure of "12" printed in 1921 sits a year later than his first appearance
   in the 1911-12 volume. Either the volume year and the roster year overlap, or the figure is
   approximate. Not resolved; noted so nobody later reads a contradiction into it.

AND ONE HUMAN DETAIL THAT IS DOCUMENTED RATHER THAN INFERRED: W. S. MAGUIRE is the Physical
Director alongside Cross at Montreal's North Branch through 1911-1916, is General Secretary at
Brandon, Manitoba in 1918-19, and is Physical Director at VICTORIA alongside Cross again in
1920-21. The two men appear on the same branch staff on opposite coasts nine years apart.


A THIRD NAME FOR THE CUSHING TANGLE
-----------------------------------
"Central Br., 127 Drummond St., Chairman, LEMUEL CUSHING" in both 1914-15 and 1915-16. This
project already has a Lemuel Cushing taking boys to Lake Saint-Joseph in 1892 and a W. E.
Cushing on the 1892 committee, and yesterday's inventory added a Charles Cushing as the YMCA's
corresponding member for Quebec in 1887. A Lemuel Cushing chairing Montreal's Central Branch
twenty-two years after the Lake Saint-Joseph trip is either the same man late in life or a
younger relative. NEITHER IS ESTABLISHED HERE. It is a name, a post and two years.


QUERIES RUN
-----------
googleapis.com/books/v1/volumes with a control (429, same consumer project as yesterday);
books.google.com and google.com/search?tbm=bks (302 to /sorry/); babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt
(403 Cloudflare); umedia.lib.umn.edu/search.json bare, with set_spec, and with facets[] forms;
archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources (202, empty body);
dmQuery on p16022coll351 for: everything (173), CISOSEARCHALL Kanawana (17 pages, 11 volumes),
Montreal (2,742 pages, 124 volumes — the OCR control), Holliday (243), Jubilee (112),
"Holliday Montreal Boys" (67), and exact-phrase "Harold C. Cross" (39);
dmGetItemInfo on page records 40653, 10775, 5588, 9511, 5075, 4630, 6211, 8974, 3834, 34456,
15084, 34016 and the seventeen Kanawana pages.


==========================================================================================
SECOND PASS, THE SAME DAY — THE 1900-1906 MONTREAL BLOCK, AND WHAT 1962 ACTUALLY SAYS
==========================================================================================

W. H. BALL'S DEPARTURE, NARROWED FROM FIVE YEARS TO ONE BOUNDARY
  1900     "Montreal ... Phys. Director, W. H. Ball, Jr."
  1901     "Phys.Director. W. H Ball, Jr. / Asst. Phys. Dir., Arthur B. Dawson"
  1902     "Phys. Director. J. E. Merritt / Asst. Phys. Dir., Arthur B. Dawson"
Merritt succeeded Ball directly at the 1901/1902 boundary; the assistant stayed through it.

THE TRAP, RECORDED BECAUSE IT NEARLY WORKED. An exact-phrase search for "W. H. Ball" returns
44 pages across the series, and the hits in the 1902, 1904-05, 1905-06 and 1906-07 volumes are
THREE OTHER MEN: a W. H. Ball at Brooklyn's Prospect Park Branch, one at Springfield,
Massachusetts, and one who is DETROIT's Physical Director for at least two years. Following the
name would have kept Montreal's Ball in post until 1907 and been wrong by six years. The answer
came from reading Montreal's own block in each volume. A related hazard on the same pages:
Montreal's assistant physical director in 1902-03 and 1903-04 is HAROLD G. BEALL.

FINDING THE MONTREAL BLOCK AT ALL IS THE FIDDLY PART. Each volume prints the same men twice —
an international-committee membership list and the Directory of Associations — and a search for
"D. A. Budge" returns both. The committee list is the one that runs "D. A. Budge ... Montreal,
Que. / G. H. Harrower / A. Kingman / L. H. Packard"; the directory is the one that runs
"Montreal ... Pres. / Gen. Secy. / Asst. / Phys. Director". Searching for "J. E. Merritt"
lands on the directory page directly and is the faster route.

THE MONTREAL BOYS' WORK LINE, WHICH IS THE OFFICE THAT RAN THE CAMP
  1900        "Junior Dept.,"          NO NAME PRINTED
  1901, 1902  "Boys' Dept., John Brown"
  1902-03     "Boys' Secy,"            NO NAME PRINTED
  1903-04     "Boys' Work Director, Cecil M. Daggett"
  1904-05     "Boys' Work Dir.,"       NO NAME PRINTED
  1905-06     "Boys' Work Dir., W. A. Maclaren"
CECIL M. DAGGETT occurs nowhere else in this project. A blank line is NOT a vacant office —
these rosters leave lines blank routinely, Montreal's Educational Director among them.

AND A CORRECTION TO THIS PROJECT'S OWN TRANSCRIPTION. f_4967 quotes the 1906 Montreal block as
ending "Phys. Dir., J. E. MERRITT. Asst. Phys. Dir., William Sovereign." The Minnesota scan of
the same volume gives the identical list and then ONE MORE LINE, which is the last on the page:
"Boys' Work Dir., W. A. Maclaren". So 1906's boys' work post was filled, and Holliday — listed
that year as a plain assistant — was the junior man under Maclaren rather than a man appearing
from nowhere in 1907. The two then trade places twice: Holliday takes boys' work in 1907-08;
by 1909 he is an assistant again and MACLAREN is secretary of the Fairmount Avenue Branch; and
by 1910-11 HOLLIDAY is secretary of the Fairmount Avenue Branch. Entry years: Maclaren 04,
Holliday 06.

WHY 1962 RETURNED NO "KANAWANA" HIT
The 1962 volume IS in the collection (record 34925) and IS searchable — it returns "Kamp" (in
"Kamp Kiamesha", a New Jersey camp), "Otoreke" and "Hubbard". Its Quebec block reads:
"... Staff Training & Development, Hedley G. Dimock / PROGRAM, A. ROSS SEAMAN / Public
Relations, Gerald H. Wright / Director Camp Otoreke, Clarence J. McGerrigle."
SEAMAN IS THERE, in the same slot he holds in 1961 and 1963. The roster prints his title as bare
"Program" that year and drops the camp's name, while Otoreke's line on the very next row keeps
its own. The null is one word in one year; the 1959-1968 run is unbroken.

The 1962 employed-officers list also gives "McKay, C. R., Kitchener, Ont., Adult Program, 52" —
Colin R. McKay at Kitchener the year before he turns up at Montreal running Otoreke — and
"McGerrigle, C. J., Montreal, Que., Met. Bd., Dir. Camp Otoreke, 27".

STILL UNCHECKED: the 1885 (record 11848) and 1889 (13974) volumes, both in the collection, both
unread. They are the last two nineteenth-century holes in this series.


==========================================================================================
THIRD PASS — THE WAR YEARS' MONTREAL BLOCK, WHICH THE FIRST PASS DID NOT REACH
==========================================================================================

THE ONE THAT MATTERS: THE CAMP'S DIRECTOR AND CENTRAL'S BOYS' WORKER ARE THE SAME MAN, 1916-1919
  Year Book, Central Br., Boys:  John G. MacKinnon in 1915-16, 1916-17, 1917-18 and 1918-19.
  Annual reports (already held): MacKinnon directs Kanawana in 1916, 1917, 1918 (to 3 August)
                                 and 1919 -- "Mr. MacKinnon has been appointed Director for
                                 this season."
Two publications with no view of each other, one man, the same four years. By the 1920-21
volume the post has passed to R. E. G. Davis and MacKinnon is Industrial Secretary.
THIS QUALIFIES THE CAUTION WRITTEN IN THE FIRST PASS. It remains true that a branch boys' post
and an association-level Boys' Work directorship are two different offices. But for 1916-1919
the question of which one the camp answered to has an answer, and it makes the Central Branch
boys' post the first place to look for Hollinshead (1910-12) and D. J. Evans (1912-14).

HOLLIDAY VANISHES, 1917 TO 1922
  1911-12 to 1916-17   North Br., 2300 Park Ave., Secy., W. J. Holliday
  1917-18              North Br., Secy., THOMAS S. SMITH   -- Holliday not in the Montreal block
  1918-19              North Br., Secy., Thomas S. Smith   -- Holliday not in the Montreal block
  1922 (already held)  North Br., 2300 Park Ave., Secy., W. J. Holliday
A five-year hole in the middle of the career of the man the 1931 report calls the camp's first
director, opening in the last year of the war. IT IS A NULL IN ONE PUBLICATION. The far end is
soft: the 1919-20 and 1920-21 volumes were read at their North Branch and Westmount blocks, not
swept whole for the name.

NORTH BRANCH BOYS' WORKERS AFTER CROSS
  1914-15, 1915-16   Arthur L. Walsh
  1916-17            S. Burton Cuthbert
  1917-18, 1918-19   J. G. Cruickshank
  1919-20            Charles G. Hewett
  1920-21            Geoffrey Guiton, with Robert E. Blake and G. S. Mooney as assistants
Cruickshank and Hewett occur nowhere else in this project. This is Cross's branch (1911-14) and
Holliday's branch (1911-17), so the list is worth having whole; no camp connection is documented
for any of these four.

GRANT D. BRANDON, EARLIER THAN THIS PROJECT HAD HIM
  1918-19   Central Br., "Community, Grant D. Brandon"
  1920-21   association level, "Community, R. Gordon Burgoyne / Community, Grant D. Brandon"
The project's earliest sighting was the 1921 volume. He directs Kanawana in 1921, so THE 1921
CAMP DIRECTOR WAS THE ASSOCIATION'S COMMUNITY SECRETARY, not its boys' work secretary -- one
more case of the camp directorship sitting apart from the boys' work post.
KEEP APART: PERCY D. BRANDON is a different man in the same rosters -- Assistant Physical at
Central in 1915-16, Boys Physical in 1916-17 and 1917-18. Two Brandons, no established relation.

FINDING THE MONTREAL BLOCK IN THE LATER VOLUMES: an exact-phrase search for "D. A. Budge" still
works (he is Consulting Secretary into the 1920s), and "Westmount Br" is a good second probe
since the Montreal block always runs Central, North, Westmount, R. R. in that order.


==========================================================================================
FOURTH PASS — AND THIS ONE FETCHED NOTHING
==========================================================================================

Every finding below comes from YMCA of Montreal annual reports already in this project's cache,
in files marked read. The Year Book's contribution was the NAMES. Hollinshead, Lordly, Daggett
and Murray Brooks occurred nowhere in this project, so nobody could grep for them.

FROM THE 1910 ANNUAL REPORT (sgw-ymca-annual-report-1910.txt):
  "Next month Mr. K. J. HOLLINSHEAD, OF ALBION COLLEGE, MICHIGAN, will take up the Boys'
   Secretaryship, which MR. MURRAY BROOKS RESIGNED TO GO AS STRATHCONA HALL'S REPRESENTATIVE
   IN THE FOREIGN WORK IN CEYLON."
  "The Central Association will also lose, with regret, MR. HOLLIDAY'S SERVICES, AS IN THE EARLY
   FALL HE GOES AS SECRETARY TO THE FAIRMOUNT BRANCH, PREPARING THE WAY FOR THE LARGER WORK IN
   THE ANNEX, WHICH THE NEW BUILDING WILL ENTAIL."

FROM THE 1913 ANNUAL REPORT:
  "Mr. K. J. Hollinshead LEAVES ON AUGUST 1ST to take up Community Work, and will be succeeded
   by MR. D. J. EVANS, FORMERLY PROVINCIAL SECRETARY OF THE BOY SCOUTS' MOVEMENT. MR. H. A.
   LORDLY joined the Boys' Department staff in July, SUCCEEDING MR. H. W. RITTENHOUSE."

FROM THE 1914 ANNUAL REPORT (year ending 30 April 1914, so the summer of 1913):
  "The Boys' Camp at Lake Kanawana was open for July and August with 162 boys, apart from
   visitors, IN CHARGE OF MESSRS. D. J. EVANS, HAROLD CROSS, AND H. A. LORDLY FOR SUCCESSIVE
   PORTIONS OF THE SEASON."
  (The men's camp at Lake St. Joseph the same summer: H. C. Patterson, 160 men, 5 July to
   2 September.)

WHAT THAT SETTLES
  - M. G. Brooks is MURRAY BROOKS; he RESIGNED, and went to Ceylon. p_466 closed.
  - The Boys' Secretaryship: Brooks -> mid-1910 Hollinshead -> 1 Aug 1913 D. J. Evans.
  - Holliday's 1909-10 move to Fairmount was a posting to open a branch ahead of a new
    building, "with regret" — not a demotion. directors-index.md had deliberately left the
    reason open; the association supplied one.
  - HAROLD C. CROSS WAS AT KANAWANA IN 1913, twelve years before his directorship.

AND THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART, WHICH IS THE REAL LESSON
The 162-boy figure in that last quotation has been in attendance-series.md for months. It was
taken from the sentence that names three men. The number came out; the names stayed in.
A DOCUMENT MARKED "extracted" HAS BEEN READ FOR THE QUESTIONS SOMEBODY HAD AT THE TIME. That is
not the same as having been read. And the corollary is the practical rule: WHEN AN OUTSIDE
SOURCE HANDS YOU A NEW NAME FOR AN INSTITUTION THIS PROJECT ALREADY HOLDS DOCUMENTS ABOUT, GREP
THE CACHE FOR IT IMMEDIATELY, before doing anything else with it.


==========================================================================================
FIFTH PASS — THE 1885 AND 1889 VOLUMES (p_469), AND BALL AT SPRINGFIELD
==========================================================================================

1889, record 13974, page 239 (rec 13863), under "CORRESPONDING MEMBERS OF THE CONVENTION":
  "Rev. David Allen Read, Springfield, Mass. / G. D. Baker, Ass'n Train. School, [ditto] /
   WM. H. BALL, JR., [ditto] / Geo. W. Banning, [ditto] / S. E. Barrett / K. O. Bartlett /
   J. E. Canfield / F. M. Carey / A. T. Carson ..."
The ditto marks OCR as "44", "14" and "4 4". The whole run is Association Training School,
Springfield, Massachusetts.

WHY IT MATTERS: this project has Ball entering Association work in 1889 (f_4976) and Montreal
introducing him in 1892 as "the physical director, W. H. Ball Jr., A NEW MAN, FROM THE
SPRINGFIELD TRAINING SCHOOL", with 1884, 1886, 1887, 1888 and 1890 holding no W. H. Ball at all.
The 1889 volume catches him at the school in the year he entered the work. Montreal's account of
where he came from is now corroborated from OUTSIDE MONTREAL and CONTEMPORANEOUSLY.

STRONG, NOT CERTAIN. Four different W. H. Balls appear across this series (f_5273) and the
surname is common in the association. None of the others is at Springfield, and the "Jr." and
the year both match. Recorded that way.

1885 (record 11848) HOLDS NO W. H. BALL. Its only Ball is an F. D. Ball. 1890 and 1891 are still
blank and there is nothing left in this series to try for them.

FIVE MONTREAL NAMES ON THE SAME 1889 PAGE, none of them previously anywhere in this project:
  "Charles Babcock, Montreal, Que. / J. S. Hetherington / Robert S. Ross / Wm. Sloan /
   John R. Terrill" (the last OCR'd "Terrtll")
Convention volunteers, not paid officers. Grepped against the cache immediately, per the rule:
a WM. SLOAN sits on the association's EXTENSION FUND committee in the report for 1893-94, THE
CAMP'S FOUNDING YEAR, with John P. Copland under chairman Geo. H. Harrower; J. S. Hetherington
appears there only as a ten-dollar subscriber. Whether the committee's Sloan is the convention's
Sloan is NOT established, and the same report separately lists a John J. Sloan and a Geo. Sloan.


==========================================================================================
SIXTH PASS — M. G. BROOKS, FORTY YEARS FROM ONE ENTRY-YEAR FIGURE (p_470)
==========================================================================================

METHOD, BECAUSE IT IS REUSABLE. The alphabetical list of employed officers prints a two-digit
YEAR OF ENTRY INTO ASSOCIATION WORK after every name, and it does not change as the man moves.
So a single figure -- 05 for Brooks -- lets you follow one man across forty years of volumes and
tell him apart from other men of the same name. An exact-phrase search on the INVERTED form
("Brooks, M. G.") is what these lists respond to; the running form does not appear in them.

  1907-08   "Brooks, M. G., McGILL UNIV., MONTREAL, SEC, 05"
  1908-09   "Brooks, M. G., Montreal, Que., BOYS, 05"
  1909      Montreal's BOYS' WORK DIRECTOR (already held here, f_4983)
  1910      resigns "to go as Strathcona Hall's representative in the Foreign Work in Ceylon"
  1910-11   "Brooks, M. G., COLOMBO, CEYLON, Sec Int. Com., 05"
  ... and the same in 1911-12, 1912-13, 1913-14, 1915-16, 1916-17, 1917-18, 1918-19, 1919-20,
      1921-22 and 1922-23
  1934      "Brooks, M. G., TORONTO, ONT., Sec. National Council, 05"
  1938      "Brooks, M. G., BURMA, Sec World Service, 05"
  1944      SECTION IV, RETIRED SECRETARIES (as of 1 April 1945):
            "Brooks, M. G. ... Montreal, Que., Central ... 456 Pine Ave., W., Montreal, Que.
             ... March 11, 1945"
  1957      still among the retired, at 93 Berczy St., Barrie, Ont.

THE PIECE THAT MAKES THE 1910 REPORT MAKE SENSE: he was STRATHCONA HALL'S OWN SECRETARY before
he was Montreal's boys' worker. The McGill University YMCA moved into Strathcona Hall in 1905.
So "Strathcona Hall's representative in the Foreign Work" is the student association sending out
its former secretary, not a stranger it was funding.

CAUTION ON THE RETIRED LIST: its "Association" column may name the association through which a
man was PENSIONED rather than where he last served. Brooks was in Burma in 1938. Do not read
"Montreal, Que., Central" in 1945 as a return to Montreal service.

WHAT DID NOT WORK, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RETRIED: Open Library search-inside on the three name
forms. "Brooks, M. G." 934 hits, "M. G. Brooks" 346, "Murray Brooks" 190 -- all noise, the name
being far too common. The book corpus is the wrong instrument for a man with this name; the
roster, with its entry-year figure, is the right one.


==========================================================================================
SEVENTH PASS — THE SAME ENTRY-YEAR TRICK, APPLIED TO KANAWANA'S FIRST CAMP DIRECTOR
==========================================================================================

W. J. HOLLIDAY, followed on his entry-year figure of 06 through the alphabetical list of
employed officers, exact-phrase "Holliday, W. J.":

  1905-06   "Montreal, Que. Asst., 06"
  1907-08   "Montreal, Que., Boys, 06"
  1910-11   "Montreal, Fairmount, Sec, 06"
  1912-13   "Montreal, North Br., Sec, 06"
  1914-15   "Montreal, North Br., Sec, 06"
  1915-16   "Montreal, North Br., Sec, 06"
  1916-17   "Montreal, North Br., Sec, 06"
  1917-18   ABSENT
  1918-19   ABSENT
  1919-20   "SYDNEY, N. S., Sec, 06"
  1920-21   "Sydney, N. S., Sec, 06"
  1922-23   "Montreal, Que., North, Sec, 06"
  1923-24   "Montreal, Que., North, Sec, 06"

SO THE FIVE-YEAR HOLE NARROWS TO ABOUT TWO, and the destination is Cape Breton.

AND THEN THE CACHE ANSWERED THE REST. Montreal's report for the year ending 30 April 1918:
  "North Branch. -- MR. W. J. HOLLIDAY, SECRETARY, RESIGNED FOR OVERSEAS SERVICE and was
   succeeded by MR. T. S. SMITH, OF QUEBEC, ON FEBRUARY 12TH. Mr. W. S. MAGUIRE resigned as
   Physical Director ON DECEMBER 20TH, to become Secretary of the BRANDON ASSOCIATION.
   Mr. S. B. CUTHBERT retired APRIL 30TH, to enter business life. Mr. J. G. CRUIKSHANK, A
   RETURNED SOLDIER who has been doing splendid work with Mr. MacKinnon in Central, succeeds
   MR. GEO. W. O. MATTHEWS, as Boys' Work Secretary, ON MAY 1ST."

f_5279 had said war service was the obvious hypothesis and REFUSED TO RECORD IT. That refusal
was right, and the answer was in this project's own cache the whole time -- in a sentence nobody
had reason to look for until the Year Book narrowed the question to a two-year window. THAT IS
THE SHAPE OF THE WHOLE DAY: the outside source supplies the question precise enough to search
the inside source with.
GEO. W. O. MATTHEWS is new to this project entirely and the Year Book alone never showed him.

A DISTINCTION THAT MUST NOT BE LOST. The report for the year ending 30 April 1917, on the summer
of 1916, has Holliday "in charge" of a camp for a fortnight -- and it is THE MEN'S CAMP:
  "The MEN'S CAMP was open last season from July 14th to August 19th with a total attendance of
   131 ... MR. HENDERSON had charge during the two weeks in July, followed by MR. MACLAREN for
   one week, and MR. HOLLIDAY FOR THE LAST TWO WEEKS."
The BOYS' CAMP is the next paragraph: 24 June to 18 August, 175 boys, "Mr. MacKinnon acted as
Leader throughout." TWO CAMPS, ONE SEASON. Holliday's fortnight is Lake Saint-Joseph, not
Kanawana, and the phrase "had charge" invites exactly the conflation that must not happen.


==========================================================================================
EIGHTH PASS — THE WAR SERVICE LISTS, AND HOLLIDAY'S GIVEN NAME
==========================================================================================

THE SERIES CARRIES WAR-SERVICE ROSTERS THAT ARE NOT IN THE ASSOCIATION DIRECTORY AND DO NOT
ANSWER TO THE SAME SEARCHES. Two of them:

  1917-18 volume, from about page 440: "SECRETARIES AND OTHERS IN WAR SERVICE" -- United States,
  names with a posting ("Camp Sherman, Ohio", "Great Lakes, Ill.", "Eagle Hut, New York City"),
  and a second run of pages giving names IN FULL with no posting at all. Some names carry a
  prefixed dagger or cross. THE KEY WAS NOT FOUND ON ANY PAGE READ AND ITS MEANING IS NOT
  RECORDED HERE. Do not guess it.

  1918-19 volume, PAGE 434, record 15141: "OVERSEAS SECRETARIES / CANADIAN NATIONAL COUNCIL,
  JUNE 1, 1919 / Released from regular Y. M. C. A. work for this special service."

THE SECOND LIST GIVES KANAWANA'S FIRST CAMP DIRECTOR HIS GIVEN NAME:

    "HOLLIDAY, CAPT. WILLIAM J."

Every roster this project has ever seen gives him as "W. J." and nothing more. He is CAPTAIN
WILLIAM J. HOLLIDAY. And READ THE HEADING BEFORE READING THE RANK: these men were RELEASED FROM
REGULAR YMCA WORK for special service, so the ranks are those of YMCA officers attached to the
forces rather than necessarily of enlisted soldiers -- which decides whether a Canadian
Expeditionary Force file exists for him at all.

MONTREAL MEN ON THE SAME LIST, each checked against this project's own rosters rather than
assumed from a surname:
    Miller, Capt. Thomas Hicks   -- had charge of the KANAWANA season in July 1915;
                                    his given names were not held here
    Carson, Lieut. J. Morley     -- Westmount Branch secretary
    Corbett, Capt. Ed. A.        -- Gen. Secy., McGill University association, 1914-16
    Swetman, Capt. Herbert J.    -- Central Br., Social, by 1920-21
    McKay, Capt. J. G.           -- McGill Gen. Secy. 1919-20; Westmount Secy. 1911-12
    McKellar, F. J.              -- Asst. at Montreal Central in the 1907 volume
SO THE 1917-18 AND 1918-19 HOLES IN MONTREAL'S ROSTER ARE NOT ONE MAN'S ABSENCE BUT A
DEPARTMENT'S. And "Hollinshead, Kenneth J." -- Montreal's Boys' Secretary 1910 to 1913 -- is in
the 1917-18 United States list. Both of the men who ran Montreal's boys' work across the 1910s
ended in war service.

THE LIST IS CANADA-WIDE AND ABOUT A HUNDRED NAMES LONG. ONLY THE MONTREAL ONES HAVE BEEN TAKEN.
It also names the men who ran other camps in the movement in those years. p_474.

AND A NULL WORTH KEEPING: GEO. W. O. MATTHEWS, North Branch Boys' Work Secretary before
Cruickshank took the post on 1 May 1918, IS IN NO ROSTER IN THIS SERIES. Exact phrases
"Matthews, G. W. O." and "Geo. W. O. Matthews" return zero; the loose terms "Matthews" and
"Mathews" across the 1915-16 to 1919-20 volumes return only Alabama branch secretaries and
United States army camp secretaries. The likely reason is that his whole tenure fell BETWEEN TWO
ANNUAL EDITIONS -- a hypothesis, since the report never says when he started. The established
consequence is that AN ANNUAL ROSTER CANNOT SEE A MAN WHO CAME AND WENT INSIDE ONE YEAR, and the
boys' work line reconstructed from this series is incomplete by at least him.


==========================================================================================
NINTH PASS — THE WAR LISTS TESTED AGAINST HAROLD C. CROSS, AND A CONTROLLED NEGATIVE
==========================================================================================

Cross's three-volume absence (1915-16, 1916-17, 1917-18) had war service as its obvious
hypothesis. The two war-service rosters in this series would catch a YMCA man who went:
  1917-18 volume: "SECRETARIES AND OTHERS IN WAR SERVICE" (United States)
  1918-19 volume, p.434: "OVERSEAS SECRETARIES, CANADIAN NATIONAL COUNCIL, JUNE 1, 1919"

HE IS ON NEITHER. Searched as exact phrases "Cross, H. C.", "Cross, Harold" and "Harold C.
Cross"; and the Canadian list's full text was read, where THE SURNAME CROSS DOES NOT OCCUR AT
ALL.

THE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES THE NULL WORTH ANYTHING. Those same lists DO name his Montreal
colleagues -- W. J. Holliday on the Canadian one, Kenneth J. Hollinshead on the United States
one -- so they reach the right institution in the right years and are not blind to Montreal.

WHAT IT RULES OUT AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It makes it unlikely he went overseas AS A YMCA
SECRETARY, the route his colleagues took. It says nothing about military enlistment, which
leaves no mark in a YMCA roster. So the Canadian Expeditionary Force personnel records are MORE
worth the effort for Cross than for Holliday, not less: an enlisted man leaves a service file,
where a YMCA officer "released from regular Y. M. C. A. work for this special service" may not.


==========================================================================================
TENTH PASS — THE WAR-SERVICE SECTION'S OWN KEY, WHICH IS ON EACH SUB-LIST'S FIRST PAGE
==========================================================================================

THE SYMBOL LEFT UNEXPLAINED IN THE EIGHTH PASS IS RESOLVED. The key was not on any of the pages
read then because IT SITS ON THE FIRST PAGE OF EACH SUB-LIST, not once at the section's front.

  record 15816 (1917-18 volume):
    "SECRETARIES OF NATIONAL WAR WORK COUNCIL / HOME FIELD / June 1, 1918 /
     (dagger) Released from Regular Y. M. C. A. Work for this Special Service"
  record 15840 (same volume, page 459):
    "SECRETARIES AND OTHERS IN WAR SERVICE / IN FOREIGN COUNTRIES / June 1, 1918 /
     (dagger) Released from Regular Y. M. C. A. Work for this Special Service"

THE DAGGER MARKS A SERVING YMCA OFFICER SENT TO WAR WORK, as against someone recruited for the
war. It OCRs as "t" or "f" prefixed to the surname.

SO KENNETH J. HOLLINSHEAD -- who carries the dagger and sits in the FOREIGN COUNTRIES list --
was abroad in YMCA war work as of 1 JUNE 1918, and was a regular officer released for it.

AND HE IS ON THE AMERICAN COUNCIL'S LIST, NOT THE CANADIAN ONE THAT CARRIES HOLLIDAY. That fits:
the 1910 Montreal report introduces him as coming "of Albion College, Michigan". The two men who
ran Montreal's boys' work across the 1910s both ended in war service, by two different national
organisations.

FORMAT NOTE THAT EXPLAINS THE EARLIER CONFUSION: the HOME FIELD list gives "Surname, Initials,
Posting" ("Ballard, J. H., Camp Merritt, N. J."); the FOREIGN COUNTRIES list gives FULL GIVEN
NAMES AND NO POSTING ("Bogardus, Rollins", "Boisen, Anton Theophilus"). A change of format inside
one running head is a change of list.

AND THE LESSON FOR ANYONE HUNTING THESE: THE SERIES PUTS SEVERAL DATED LISTS IN ONE VOLUME under
one running head. Searching for a single heading will not find them all. Walk the records
backwards from a known page until the format or the date changes.


==========================================================================================
ELEVENTH PASS — A CORRECTION, AND THE RULE THAT COMES OUT OF IT
==========================================================================================

THE 1917-18 VOLUME CARRIES ITS OWN CANADIAN LIST, and Holliday is on it:
  record 15785, page 404: "OVERSEAS SECRETARIES / CANADIAN NATIONAL COUNCIL, JUNE 1, 1918 /
  (symbol) Released from regular Y. M. C. A. work for this special service."
Montreal has him succeeded at the North Branch on 12 FEBRUARY 1918. SO HE LEFT BETWEEN
12 FEBRUARY AND 1 JUNE 1918, and is on the Canadian overseas lists of BOTH 1918 and 1919.

WHICH MEANS THIS FILE AND f_5296 WERE WRONG, IN A WAY WORTH NAMING. Both said Holliday was
"ABSENT from the 1917-18 and 1918-19 volumes". HE IS IN BOTH. He is absent from their
ALPHABETICAL LIST OF PAID OFFICERS and from the MONTREAL DIRECTORY, and present in their
war-service sections.

WHY THE SEARCH MISSED HIM: THE LISTS USE DIFFERENT NAME FORMS.
  paid officers        "Holliday, W. J."
  Canadian overseas    "Holliday, Capt. William J."
  US home field        "Ballard, J. H., Camp Merritt, N. J."     (surname, initials, posting)
  US foreign countries "Bogardus, Rollins"                        (full given names, no posting)
An exact-phrase search on one form searches ONE LIST.

THE RULE: NAME THE LIST, NEVER THE VOLUME. "He is not in the alphabetical list of paid officers"
is a statement that can be true and checked. "He is not in the volume" is a claim about a dozen
lists at once and needs a dozen searches behind it. The same slip is what made the war-service
key look missing in the eighth pass -- it was on a page the search form never reached.


==========================================================================================
TWELFTH PASS — RULE 37 CATCHES ITS AUTHOR, AND CROSS WENT OVERSEAS AFTER ALL
==========================================================================================

Within minutes of writing "name the list, never the volume", it overturned the session's
strongest negative.

THE CANADA SECTION carries a table headed "SECRETARIES OF THE NATIONAL COUNCIL", giving each man
a role -- General Secretary, Boys' Work Secretary (TAYLOR STATTEN), Railroad Secretary -- and
then a long run of names under the role "OVERSEAS REPRESENTATIVE", carried down by ditto marks.

  1914-15 (rec 6209)   Forgie present. NO Cross -- he is General Secretary at Charlottetown.
  1915-16 (rec 8972)   "... C. T. Sharpe / Elwood G. Duncan / Fred J. Smith /
                        Frederick G. Mara / H.C.Cross / THOMAS H. MILLER / F. E. Wilson ..."
  1916-17 (rec 3831)   "... James Clarke / H.C.Cross / H. H. Dennison / Elwood G. Duncan /
                        George Stuart Easton / William Fingland / George W. Fisher /
                        A. W. FORGIE ..."

SO HAROLD C. CROSS WENT OVERSEAS WITH THE CANADIAN YMCA FROM ABOUT 1915, and the war years in his
biography are no longer a hole. THOMAS H. MILLER -- who had charge of the Kanawana season in July
1915 -- is in the same run, as is A. W. Forgie.

WHY IT WAS MISSED, AND IT IS NOT THE SAME REASON AS LAST TIME.
  - f_5305 recorded that Cross is on NEITHER war-service list, CONTROLLED by the fact that both
    lists name Holliday and Hollinshead. THE CONTROL WAS SOUND. THE INFERENCE WAS NOT: two lists
    naming his colleagues does not make two lists exhaustive. This is a third list.
  - AND THE OCR HID HIM. The entry is printed "H.C.Cross" WITH NO SPACES. The exact phrases
    "Cross, H. C.", "Cross, Harold" and "Harold C. Cross" ALL MISS IT. Only a loose single-word
    search for "Cross" across the three volumes found him.
  - This project already had rule 22 -- "a multi-word grep returning zero may be a fact about the
    whitespace." It cost a wrong conclusion anyway.

RULE 37a: A NEGATIVE ABOUT A PERSON NEEDS A LOOSE SINGLE-TOKEN SEARCH BEFORE IT IS RECORDED,
however many exact forms have been tried. Every exact form shares the assumption that the source
spaces a name the way you do.

AND A TOOL EFFECT WORTH KNOWING, FOUND WHILE FIXING THIS. scripts/verify/citation_aim.py builds
its stopword list BY DOCUMENT FREQUENCY ACROSS THE WHOLE KB. This session wrote twenty-odd facts
about this series, nearly all of them saying "volume", and "VOLUME" CROSSED THE CUTOFF -- which
broke two citations in canoe-trips.md and camp-perrot.md that had been passing on that one shared
word. NEITHER ARTICLE WAS EDITED; the knowledge base moved under them. A citation resting on one
ordinary shared word is fragile by construction. f_5309.


==========================================================================================
THIRTEENTH PASS — THE 1957-1968 NULL, TESTED THREE WAYS AFTER 37a
==========================================================================================

Rule 37a had just cost a wrong conclusion about Cross, so the session's other big null was
re-tested rather than trusted.

1. THE EXACT NAME. "Kanawana" -> 17 pages, 11 volumes, 1957 to 1968. As before.

2. THE WILDCARD STEM. THE ENDPOINT SUPPORTS TRUNCATION: CISOSEARCHALL^Kanaw*^all^and works and
   returns 386 pages across 69 volumes. EVERY SAMPLED ONE IS "KANAWHA" -- the West Virginia river
   and county, and a common YMCA place name (Charleston sits on it). No OCR variant of the camp
   turned up. ("Kanawana*" returns the same 17; "Kanawan" returns 0.)

3. THE PLACE NAMES, since a camp can be listed by where it is rather than what it is called:
     "Lac Wilson"    0 pages in the entire series
     "Lake Wilson"   0
     "Laurentian"    0
     "Sauveur"       9 pages, ALL of them St. Sauveur de Montagut in the Ardeche, or a Henri
                     Sauveur in Belgium. NOT ONE is Saint-Sauveur, Quebec.

SO THE CAMP IS NOT IN THIS SERIES BEFORE 1957 UNDER ITS NAME, UNDER A PLAUSIBLE MANGLING OF ITS
NAME, OR UNDER WHERE IT IS. The structural explanation stands and is the thing to record: the
roster began listing camps as posts within a metropolitan board's staff in the late 1950s. The
silence is about that practice, not about a camp that had been running sixty years by then.

WORTH KEEPING FOR ITS OWN SAKE: THIS ENDPOINT DOES WILDCARDS. That is the tool rule 37a asks for
when a name might be mangled, and it was not known here until now.


==========================================================================================
FOURTEENTH PASS — THE DIRECTORS SWEEP, AND THE COLLECTION DOES NOT STOP IN 1982
==========================================================================================

CORRECTION FIRST. This file and f_5263 describe the collection as the Year Book series "running
1877 to 1982", taken from the titles that came back in one enumeration. IT ALSO HOLDS YMCA
DIRECTORIES FOR AT LEAST 1996 (rec 17305), 2000 (47077), 2001 (41677) AND 2002 (32873), OCR'd and
searchable like the rest. They are UNITED STATES directories, so Canadian camps do not appear and
the 1957-1968 Kanawana null is unaffected -- what they are good for is following a person OUT of
Canada. Same species of error as "name the list, never the volume": a claim about a collection's
extent taken from sampled titles rather than from its date range.

RAN EVERY KNOWN KANAWANA DIRECTOR'S SURNAME AS A LOOSE SEARCH (per 37a). Ereaux and Twynam return
zero. The rest returned, and three paid:

R. H. HANAGAN IS RONALD HANAGAN, and the proof needs no inference across sources. The 1941 and
1943 volumes print the SAME POST TWICE:
    branch directory, Central Br.:  "Physical, Oscar L. Pearson ... BOYS, RONALD HANAGAN"
    alphabetical list, same volume: "HANAGAN, R. H., Montreal, Que., Central, Boys, 29"
His year of entry is 1929 and the career starts in Ontario: the 1929-30 volume gives
"Gait [Galt]. ... Physical, J. W. McVicar / BOYS, RONALD HANAGAN". rh-hanagan.md opened with the
words "This article's subject is initials" and carried the given name as a CRITICAL open question.
The middle initial is still unaccounted for.

OSCAR L. PEARSON IS ONE MAN FROM 1912, and this closes most of a question raised two passes ago.
"Pearson, O. L." carries the entry-year figure 12 in every volume:
    1913-14   Toronto, West End., Asst. Ph. Dir., 12
    1921-22   Ottawa, Ont., Physical, 12
    1922-23   Toronto, Ont., Central, Physical, 12
    1943      Montreal, Que., Central, Physical, 12
So the "Pearson, Capt. Oscar L." of the 1919 overseas list and the Montreal Central physical
director of 1941-43 are ONE MAN -- a physical director of seven years' standing in 1919 is exactly
who gets released for overseas service, and the figure carries through unchanged. The 1958 camp
safety editorial in Canadian Camping Magazine is joined by NAME ALONE and is now the economical
reading rather than the speculative one: entering the work in 1912 puts his birth about 1888-1892
and his age in 1958 in the late sixties.

BRUCE NETHERWOOD IN MASSACHUSETTS, DATED. bruce-netherwood.md knew he moved to Massachusetts YMCA
camping after leaving Kanawana in 1994 and did not know where. The directories give
"NETHERWOOD, BRUCE, EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR" of the RESIDENT CAMPING DIVISION, SOUTH SHORE YMCA,
Sandwich, Massachusetts, in 1996, 2000, 2001 and 2002. INSTITUTIONAL FACT ONLY -- name, title,
employer. The directories also carry organisational phone, fax and email; those are not recorded
and should not be.

THE ENTRY-YEAR FIGURE IS THE BEST INSTRUMENT IN THIS SERIES and it has now settled four separate
identity questions in one session: Brooks, Holliday, Hanagan and Pearson.


==========================================================================================
FIFTEENTH PASS — THE 1945-1957 MONTREAL BLOCK, WHICH THE ANNUAL REPORTS LEAVE BLANK
==========================================================================================

The collection holds a near-complete run for this stretch (1949 missing): 24768=1945, 19116=1946,
43814=1947, 28960=1948, 27959=1950, 33718=1951, 46083=1952, 29289=1953, 37438=1954, 48058=1955,
45418=1956, 45747=1957. FINDING THE MONTREAL PAGE: "Otoreke" does not work before 1958 (see the
spelling note below) -- search "VERDUN", which is a Montreal branch and lands on the Quebec block.

HAROLD C. CROSS'S TITLES, WHICH HIS ARTICLE HAS WANTED SINCE FEBRUARY:
  1927-28  alphabetical list: "Cross, H. C., Montreal, Que., WESTMOUNT, SEC, 12"
  1945     alphabetical list: "Cross, H. C., Montreal, Que, Met., ACTING SEC, 12"
  1948     branch directory:  "Metro. Bd. ... PROGRAM, HAROLD C. CROSS / Boys, Roy D. Locke"
  1950     same
  1951     same
  1953     RETIRED SECRETARIES: "Cross, H. C. ... Montreal Que Met. Bd. ...
                                 RETIRED MARCH 1, 1953"
He is in the Retired Secretaries section of the 1953, 1957, 1958, 1959, 1961, 1962, 1963, 1965,
1966, 1967, 1968 and 1969 volumes, at Montreal in 1953 and BAIE D'URFE by 1959. A man leaves that
list when he dies, SO HE WAS ALIVE INTO 1969 -- independent of the 1971 photograph that was the
only prior evidence. Entry 1912 to retirement 1953 is a FORTY-ONE-YEAR CAREER and implies a birth
about 1885-1892, the first age estimate this project has had for him.
ACTING SECRETARY OF THE METROPOLITAN ASSOCIATION IN 1945 is the highest office ever documented for
him, and PROGRAM SECRETARY 1948-1951 is what he was while writing the 1951 centennial history.

ROY D. LOCKE, entry year 44: "Met. Bd., Boys" in 1950, 1951 and 1953; "Westmount, Exec" by 1955;
"Metro., Financial Devel." in 1969; "Metro, Asst. and Dir., Operations" in 1973. All of which
corroborates directors-index.md's account from the annual reports, and adds the entry year.

AND A SPELLING THAT COST TWO VOLUMES. The 1951 and 1953 blocks read "DIR. CAMP OTEREKE, Clarence
J. McGerrigle" -- WITH AN E. That is why a search for "Otoreke" returns nothing before 1958, and
why this project briefly believed the camp first appears in this series in 1958. A WILDCARD ON THE
STEM DOES NOT HELP WHEN THE ERROR IS INSIDE THE WORD. Same failure as "H.C.Cross" run together,
in a different dress. McGerrigle's documented Otoreke directorship now runs 1951-1961.


==========================================================================================
SIXTEENTH PASS — THE WAR ROSTERS ARE ONLY TWO VOLUMES, AND THE SECOND WAR IS DIFFERENT
==========================================================================================

p_474 asked whether a volume other than 1918-19 carries a Canadian overseas list. IT DOES NOT.
The phrase that keys these rosters, "Released from regular Y. M. C. A. work for this special
service", occurs in the 1917-18 AND 1918-19 VOLUMES AND NOWHERE ELSE IN THE SERIES.

THE 1916-17 "War Service" HITS ARE A FALSE LEAD and worth naming so nobody re-chases them: both
are ordinary prose, in the preface ("all leaders were on double duty owing to the extra war
service") and in a committee statement ("students who left college for various forms of war
service"). Not a roster.

CONSEQUENCE FOR HOLLIDAY: he is on both dated lists, 1 June 1918 and 1 June 1919, which bounds
the START of his service with the Montreal report's 12 February 1918 succession -- but there is
no third list, so his RETURN is dated only by his turning up at Sydney, Nova Scotia in the
1919-20 volume's alphabetical list.

AND THE SECOND WAR USES A DIFFERENT CONVENTION ENTIRELY. From the 1940s volumes there is no
separate roster: men on war service are marked IN THE ALPHABETICAL LIST ITSELF, with "War
Service" standing where an association would normally go --
    "Hall, A. M., War Service, 42"
    "Peart, H. W., War Service, ..."
So a second-war serviceman is found by reading the ORDINARY roster, and the entry-year figure
still travels with him. Anyone chasing Kanawana's wartime staff of the 1940s should search that
way rather than looking for a list that does not exist.


==========================================================================================
SEVENTEENTH PASS — THE 1941 MONTREAL BLOCK, WHICH HOLDS THREE MEN THIS SESSION HAS TRACED
==========================================================================================

    "Montreal, 1441 Drummond St., Metro. Bd. ... President, Gerald W. Birks /
     General Secretary, JOHN W. BEATON[dagger] / ACTING GENERAL SECRETARY, HAROLD C. CROSS /
     Business, Clarence M. McCulley / UNEMPLOYMENT, WILLIAM J. HOLLIDAY[dagger] /
     Office, James A. C. Hastings
     Central Br. ... Membership, William H. White / PROGRAM, MURRAY G. BROOKS /
     Dormitory, Reginald S. Cuffe / Physical, OSCAR L. PEARSON /
     Assistant Physical, Kalman Vizely / BOYS, RONALD HANAGAN / Building Boys, Harold Potter"

ONE PAGE CARRIES FIVE OF THIS SESSION'S PEOPLE.

CROSS IS ACTING GENERAL SECRETARY IN 1941 AND STILL IN 1944, not just 1945 -- four years running
the association, and the reason is on the same line: BEATON, the General Secretary, carries a
dagger, and THE PAGE'S OWN FOOTER READS "See alphabetical list of those in Y.M.C.A. War services
following alphabetical Roster of Employed Officers, page 258." NATURAL READING, NOT A PROVEN KEY:
that list was not found on the pages read, so the dagger's meaning comes from the cross-reference
and is recorded as such.

HOLLIDAY IS STILL AT MONTREAL IN 1941, thirty-six years after his first appearance in 1905-06,
where this project's previous latest sighting was 1923-24. His post is "UNEMPLOYMENT" -- a
Depression portfolio nothing else here has attached to anyone. HIS GIVEN NAME IS PRINTED IN FULL
A SECOND TIME, INDEPENDENTLY of the 1919 overseas list: "William J. Holliday" here, "Holliday,
Capt. William J." there, twenty-two years apart. And he carries the dagger too, so THE MAN WHO
WENT OVERSEAS IN 1918 APPEARS TO HAVE GONE AGAIN AT ABOUT SIXTY.

BROOKS CAME HOME. The India arc ends at the 1935 volume and this project had him retiring in 1945
"credited to Montreal Central", with a caution that the column might name where a man was
PENSIONED rather than where he served. THE CAUTION WAS UNNECESSARY: he is Central Branch's
PROGRAM secretary in 1941, back under the same given name the 1910 report used when it announced
his resignation for Ceylon thirty-one years earlier. By 1943 the post has passed to Alfred J.
Davis. Strathcona Hall -> Montreal boys' work -> Colombo -> Toronto -> Burma -> MONTREAL CENTRAL
-> retirement 1945, from the association he began with in 1905.

A NOTE ON THIS VOLUME'S DATE. It is catalogued 1941 but its alphabetical list contains entry
years of 42 and USO postings, so the catalogue year is soft here as everywhere in this series.
